title: CUDA driver compatibility quick journal
content:
Goal: capture quick reproducer breadcrumbs and hypotheses for the CI agent that started failing with repeated OOMs and "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" errors.

Context (symptoms):
- In CI/runtime: intermittent OOM during model warmup (batch size 1), but only on certain runners.
- Logs also show: "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" and on some runs: "cuDNN library not found: libcudnn.so.8".
- Local dev laptop (NVIDIA 520 driver, CUDA 11.8 toolchain) works fine; CI images use nvidia/cuda:12.1-base by default.

Short timeline of attempts / commands tried (timestamps local):
- 2025-02-18 09:12 — initial repro on ubuntu-22.04 runner (aws/g4dn-like): nvidia-smi returned driver 510.x.
  Command: nvidia-smi
  Output snippet: "Driver Version: 510.54.03    CUDA Version: 11.6"

- 2025-02-18 09:20 — quick check from inside container image used by CI:
  Command: docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:12.1-base nvidia-smi
  Result: "Driver Version: 510.54.03    CUDA Version: 12.1" -> mismatch: host driver 510 doesn't fully support runtime 12.1 but nvidia/cuda image reports runtime version 12.1 (container-side toolkit).

- 2025-02-19 11:05 — Python/CUDA checks inside failing job:
  Commands: |
    python -c 'import torch,sys; print(torch.__version__); print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.is_available())'
  Output: |
    2.1.0
    12.1
    True
  Note: torch reports cuda 12.1 but that doesn't guarantee driver compatibility.

- 2025-02-20 14:40 — ldd on libtorch to check linked cuda libs inside the conda env:
  Command: ldd $(python -c "import torch;import os;print(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(torch.__file__),'lib','libtorch.so'))") | grep cuda || true
  Observed: some libs linked to /usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs/libcuda.so -> stub present but actual driver ABI mismatch possible.

- 2025-02-21 09:30 — check host driver package info:
  Commands: cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version || dpkg -l | grep nvidia
  Output: "NVRM version: NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module  510.54.03  Wed Jul 14 2024"

- 2025-02-22 10:00 — tried reproducer with explicit older CUDA runtime image:
  Command: docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime nvidia-smi && python -c 'import torch;print(torch.version.cuda)'
  Result: driver still 510.x, runtime 11.8, torch prints 11.8 -> fewer compatibility warnings but OOM still sometimes appears.

Concrete error snippets captured from runs:
- "RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.20 GiB (GPU 0; 14.76 GiB total capacity; 12.34 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free; 1.00 GiB cached)"
- "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" (observed in python startup logs once when image was 12.1 but host driver 510)
- "ImportError: libcudnn.so.8: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Host driver is too old for some of the runtime/toolkit combinations used by our images (12.x images) -> occasional ABI issues or silently reduced functionality leading to higher memory usage and OOM.
2) Multiple libcuda.so stubs present (container stubs vs host libcuda) and LD_LIBRARY_PATH picks up wrong one -> symbol mismatches at runtime.
3) cuDNN mismatches: image/conda env expects libcudnn.so.8 but device has a system-installed cuDNN 7.x or nothing -> falls back causing larger workspace allocations or fails to use optimized kernels.
4) Memory leak in our init code (less likely given reproducibility across small tests) combined with driver/runtime mismatch amplifies OOM frequency.

Notes on what matters for compatibility (reminder):
- The NVIDIA driver on the host provides the actual kernel-level support; the CUDA toolkit/runtime in the container can be newer but must be compatible with the host driver (there's a max supported compute/runtime version per driver version).
- libcuda.so (driver API) is provided by host; libcudnn, libcublas etc typically come from the image/env.
- Stubs in /usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs are placeholders; if ldd resolves to stubs, the runtime may be routing to host driver at link-time which is OK — but stubs + incompatible host driver => runtime errors.

Next reproduction steps to try (tickets/CI changes):
- Matrix job: run simple torch reproduce on runners with explicit docker images 11.8, 12.0, 12.1 and record nvidia-smi output and python torch.version.cuda. (INF-2143 test matrix).
- In failing CI job, insert quick diagnostics at job start: nvidia-smi; cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version; ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda*; env | grep LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Save artifacts.
- Swap to base image nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime for the task that allocates the most memory and see if failure rate drops to zero. If so, strong signal driver/runtime mismatch.
- On a repro runner, try updating host driver to 535 (if allowed) and retest. Commands to apply/update driver (note: need reboot):
    sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
    sudo reboot
  (Confirm driver post-reboot with nvidia-smi)

Quick commands to help triage going forward:
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,name,memory.total --format=csv
- docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:12.1-base nvidia-smi || true
- python -c 'import torch,sys; print(sys.executable); print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory if torch.cuda.is_available() else "no-gpu")'
- ldd $(python -c "import torch,os;print(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(torch.__file__),'lib','libc10.so'))") | grep cudnn || true

Observed weirdness to flag:
- On one runner, dpkg showed both nvidia-driver-510 and 525 partially installed (dkms warnings) -> potential conflicting modules loaded. Command to check: dkms status.
- Some containers include /usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs/libcuda.so which ldd resolves; but that file is intentionally a stub and can mask missing host lib at link-time.

Quick notes for whoever picks this up:
- Primary suspect = driver too old for the container/runtime (host-driver < required for CUDA 12.x). Start by reproducing with 11.8 runtime image; if that stabilizes, we either pin CI images to 11.8 or coordinate host driver upgrades.
- Collect artifacts (nvidia-smi, /proc/driver/nvidia/version, env, ldd outputs) for a few failed runs before changing infra so we have evidence.

References and reading:
- NVIDIA driver/CUDA compatibility doc (internal link): https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/cuda-compatibility/index.html
- GH issue with similar symptoms: https://github.com/redwood/repro-gpu-ops/issues/72

Unresolved questions:
- Who controls the runner images and can we get a driver upgrade window? (ping infra/SRE)
- Are any jobs explicitly relying on CUDA runtime features only present in 12.x? (ask owners)

Action items (owner tags):
- @Ethan Moore: add diagnostic steps in CI job template (INF-2143) — due 2025-02-25.
- @Lina Gomez: try reproducer on staging runner after switching image to 11.8 runtime — due 2025-02-26.
- Me (Priya): coordinate with infra on driver upgrade window and collect pre-upgrade artifacts.

Scratchy notes / one-liners to include in ticket: 
- "Driver 510.x + container runtime 12.1 -> 'insufficient driver' warnings; try 11.8 image or upgrade host driver to >= 525/535.
- Check for multiple libcuda stubs; ensure LD_LIBRARY_PATH not pointing to $CONDA_PREFIX/lib before /usr/lib (can expose mismatched stubs).

End of journal entry (rough).
